episodes.title: Intake to a trackable job
episodes.description: Create one synthetic cleaning request and watch the landed intake workflow produce one customer, one job, three tasks, and one queued delivery without a duplicate record.
captions: Start in a clean local workspace backed by the landed Hive intake application.
Enter a synthetic request with a stable source ID and the service details the operator actually received.
Submit once: the application records one customer and one job, with three open tasks and one pending delivery.
The job card keeps source identity, task state, requested date, and delivery state together for operator follow-through.

episodes.title: Move a job through task completion
episodes.description: Use the landed job checklist to move a synthetic job from new to in-progress to complete, showing that task state persists in the same local workspace.
captions: A new synthetic job begins with all three service-operation tasks open.
Completing the first task moves the job into in-progress while the remaining work stays visible.
Complete the second task and the same job remains in-progress with one action left.
Completing the final task changes the job to complete; the customer and source record stay linked.

episodes.title: Retry only the selected delivery
episodes.description: Create two synthetic jobs and use the PR #10513 selected-event retry path: retrying one job delivers only that event, leaving the unrelated queued job untouched until the operator processes it.
captions: Two synthetic jobs are queued independently, each with its own durable delivery event.
Choose Retry delivery on the newest job: the UI sends that event ID to the selected-process path.
Only the chosen job is delivered and appears in the local notification feed; the other event remains pending.
The normal Deliver next notification action can then process the remaining due event without duplicating the first.
